claims.title: Final model and child isolation remain unqualified after successful no-model strict-profile probe
claims.disposition: The earlier no-model strict-profile probe alone was insufficient, but final v5 supplies an actual authenticated model invocation and a returned delegated-child report under the same named permission profile. This supersedes the claim that final qualification consists only of the no-model probe. Fresh-child lifecycle trace provenance remains limited as explicitly recorded below.

evidence.observation: Actual docker exec invokes codex exec with ignore-user-config, ignore-rules, ephemeral, strict-config, model gpt-6.1-sol, high effort, named qore-trial profile, root deny/minimal reads/input read/output write/network false, no login shell and app/plugin/memory/MCP restrictions.
Actual thread/turn events and completed MCP listing tool calls; resources and resourceTemplates arrays are empty.
Parent actually reads child-probe.json, verifies decoded source-byte integrity, writes final combined report and ends a model turn with nonzero usage. Exit receipt is 0.

Returned child report retains contract bytes with SHA256, canary read failures, AF_INET socket creation EPERM, complete 12-name inventory and two empty actual MCP listing outcomes. Its initial socket exception is preserved rather than hidden.

The actual sandbox consumer reads source bytes and hashes them; both harmless outside canaries and undeclared paths are absent, input mutation fails, output write succeeds, and network returns PermissionError.

Same disposable image/security profile without the inner command sandbox runs as UID1000, successfully reads both harmless canary paths and connects to 1.1.1.1:443. This rules out treating negative probes as evidence solely of an inherently disconnected container.

claims.necessary_condition_status: Observed scoped filesystem/network/tool outcomes and returned child capability report. Raw native child spawn/fork lifecycle is not retained; child freshness is corroborated by the parent spawn_response report and child visible-context statement rather than an independently inspectable spawn event.

Actual parent MCP calls are empty, child report agrees, and the complete observed tool names contain no search/fetch/browser/connector-specific tool. No concrete alternate answer-retrieval violation is demonstrated.

mechanical_checks.live_container_reinspection: UNAVAILABLE: v5 qualification container was already removed; no mutation or model call attempted.

configuration_and_consumption.outer_container: Saved docker wire args drop ALL capabilities, enable no-new-privileges and selected seccomp, no host volume mounts or privileged flag. Saved inspect-derived environment records user node, mounts=[], cap_drop ALL, bridge network. Launcher asserts no mounts/privileged/cap-add. No daemon/sysctl change appears in the launcher.
configuration_and_consumption.seccomp: Default-deny profile includes a final allow block for clone/unshare/mount/umount2/pivot_root to permit nested unprivileged namespace setup. This is broader outer namespace support, not the command-network denial mechanism. UID1000/cap-drop/no-newpriv and the inner Codex sandbox are material boundaries.
configuration_and_consumption.managed_requirements: Launcher writes /etc/codex/requirements.toml using docker exec --user root and chmod 0644; environment receipt retains exact managed restriction bytes including an empty MCP server allowlist. This is producer/wire evidence, not a live verifier restat.
configuration_and_consumption.same_launcher: trial_runtime.py CONFIGS and launch flags match v5 receipts. run_one.py stages only prepared/worker, uses this launcher, and compares actual post-input path/digest list to the frozen manifest. operator-freeze hashes match.
configuration_and_consumption.network_transport: Outer bridge and authenticated model transport remain active. The tested command socket is denied before connect; the entire container is not offline.
configuration_and_consumption.tools: Observed parent and child ALL_TOOLS each contain 12 names including generic MCP helpers and image_gen__imagegen. Generic helpers are not connector-specific tools; actual listings are empty. No resource fetch or image generation invocation occurs.
configuration_and_consumption.imagegen_assessment: Visible image generation is a residual service capability. Its name/presence alone does not establish access to repository history, evaluator answers, arbitrary URL fetch, search or a concrete alternate answer source. It was not invoked, so no positive claim of universal service-side isolation follows.

residual_limitations: CLI JSONL contains no raw spawn/fork_turns event or child command transcript. Its two wait records have empty receiver_thread_ids. The child report exists and is actually consumed, but raw lifecycle freshness is not independently demonstrated; the child reports no substantive parent history. Retain this provenance limitation and require actual role evidence in each cell.

The complete tool inventory is recorded by model reports, rather than a signed external runtime attestation. Actual parent MCP empty results are independently present in the raw CLI events; child MCP results are retained in its report.
Finite harmless canary and socket probes establish tested outcomes, not a proof against every kernel exploit, process-interface route, hidden tool or service-side channel.

The saved environment receipt summarizes Docker inspect and declares Codex0.162.0; this verifier did not recreate the image or rerun a model. Image tag is mutable in principle, so per-cell image_id receipts must remain matched to the qualified image digest.
The model/high effort settings reuse the declared existing configuration; this check establishes effective requested wire values, not account billing or comprehensive provider-side behavior.
No campaign cell has begun. These capability probes are setup attempts; no pilot may be excluded or silently replaced based on later task quality.

Resource caps are provisional. The launcher bounds an outer process wait, but killing docker exec alone is not proof of instant descendant cancellation; accounting and observed overruns must remain explicit.
actions: Read-only saved-artifact checks plus a failed read-only docker inspect. No model calls, external research, client data/credential reads, repository edits or new agents. This JSON is the sole created deliverable.
